statement: For any self-map T and nonperiodic target a, the real ancestor indicator b_a(n)=1 iff some nonnegative iterate of n equals a satisfies b_a(n)=b_a(T(n))+1_(n=a), and is not a pullback fixed point. Every nonnegative real solution of this source equation dominates b_a. For any nonnegative weight w, such a solution g with Summable(w*g^2) exists if and only if Summable(w*b_a). These are known coefficient identities, kernel-checked in the shared inverse-generation module. In particular replacing a weighted ancestor-mass problem by nonexistence of a nonnegative finite-energy source solution supplies no independent lower bound. The complex-analytic norm identification and the cited literature theorems are not part of the Lean claim.
